sentences.text: This first application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail relating to FIR No.438/2022 dated 13.12.2022 registered at Police Station - Lanji, District- Balaghat (MP) for commission of the offences punishable under Section 420, 406, 34 of IPC and under Section 21(1), (2) and (3) of the Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act has knocked the portal of this Court for grant of anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: The prosecution story in short is that one Dudeshwar Mansure, resident of Village Benegaon submitted an application in writing before the SHO Police Lanji, District Balaghat alleging that his wife's house is at Benegaon.
He came to know that Krishna Nanore and his father Laxman gives double of the amount deposited with them within two months of deposit.
Krishna's sister Kavita is her acquaintance.
When he enquired about the same from Kavita, she confirmed the news.

sentences.text: money, at this, on 03.05.2022 he gave Rs.3,25,000/- cash to Kavita Hanoti at Benegaon, Kavita handed over the same in front of him to Laxman Nanore, who gave him a cheque dated 03.07.2022 of Axis Bank of Rs.6,50,000/- lakhs.
They had asked him not to present the cheque in any bank.
On 03.07.2022, when he approached Laxman Nanore to return the double amount, he refused and asked to obtain the amount from Kavita.
When he did not return his money despite several attempts, he presented the cheque in State Bank Lanjhi which stood dishonored as it could not match with the signature of Krishna Nanore.
FIR was registered.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
Complainant never gave any amount to him.

It is submitted that on 02.09.2022 his son-in-law Vinod Hanoti who is serving in Army had lodged an FIR against son of Dudeshwar Mansure and others for commission of offence under Section 395,
365, 294, 323, 506, 147, 148, 149 of IPC, Section 25, 27 of Arms Act and Section 3(i)(r)(s), 325 and 325-A of the SC/ST (POA)Act and as a counter blast of that FIR a baseless story has been manufactured and she has been falsely implicated.
There is nothing on record except the false statement of the complainant to implicate the applicant in the commission of offence.
Cheque is not issued from his account.
Therefore, it has been prayed that applicant who has no criminal past be released on anticipatory bail.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant.
I have gone through the case diary and copy of FIR lodged by the son- in-law of the applicant against Rahul Mansore and others.
Hence, considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, I am of the view that applicant may be released on anticipatory bail.
Consequently, this first anticipatory bail application under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant stands allowed.

It is directed that in the event of arrest applicant - Laxman Narnore be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Authority.
